name: Bluff Line
design_intent:
MEADOW MILE #12 — an asymmetric bluff: one big trampoline MESA on the left (a near-safe farm) and TWO smaller bubblegum/trampoline pads stepping right over the void to a far ledge that bears the prize powerup, with a contested spring throne over the first gap. The asymmetry is the hook — hold the safe mesa or commit rightward over the void to fight for the far prize. 580px gaps, no hazard.

GEOMETRY: MESA (trampoline x0..1600 top1080) / GAP1 580px (x1600..2180) / PAD1 (bubblegum x2180..2860 top1020) / GAP2 580px (x2860..3440) / FAR LEDGE (trampoline x3440..4120 top1060, bears the prize). One spring THRONE (x2320..2680 top500 h48) hangs 520px above PAD1 and offset over GAP1. Full-width lethal void (rim y1260); bounds are ASYMMETRIC by intent: left -600 (mesa gets ~600px advantaged runway), right 4620 (~500px past the far ledge = the exposed side). Bottom y1920 leaves 712-780px recovery sky.

MOVEMENT (Tuning.gd: trampoline apex 270 / bubblegum 180 / spring 480; zero-boost drift ~395 tramp / ~320 bubblegum / ~527 spring max; normal_boost_max 760 crosses a 580px gap in <0.9s @ ~24 fuel; super 2800 clears all):
- GAP1 mesa->PAD1: x1600..x2180 = 580px over void. > 527 and >> 395. NORMAL BOOST REQUIRED; miss = fall into the void. Verb: FLY.
- GAP2 PAD1->FAR LEDGE: x2860..x3440 = 580px over void. > 527. NORMAL BOOST REQUIRED; the prize is only won by committing rightward over the void. Verb: FLY.
- CLIMB to the THRONE (top500): 520px above PAD1 (1020) AND offset over GAP1. Best pad bounce (bubblegum 180) reaches y840 -> 340px short even before the offset; under-shot drops into the void. JETPACK CLIMB REQUIRED. Verb: FLY.
- RECOVER: mesa/pad/ledge bottoms (1132-1208) to bottom blast (1920) = 712-788px recovery sky (>= 650); a knock off a 680px pad or the far ledge is a shorter, less-recoverable ring-out than off the wide mesa (the asymmetry IS the risk gradient). Verb: FLY.
- Both gaps exceed a spring bounce's reach and the throne sits above spring apex, so flight is required. Vertical AND horizontal distance are load-bearing.
